conventions.selection: Bounds include both instants. The preceding actual mark supplies opening capital for a date cut. Displayed marks stay inside the selection. An opening mark alone earns no period return.
conventions.sampling: Use the last selected mark in each UTC day, Monday-to-Sunday week, month or year. The opening and final buckets can be partial. Return timestamps identify actual observations.
conventions.sessions: For daily sampling, sessionDates lists the expected UTC trading dates. The caller supplies the full calendar for the span. Only listed days produce daily closes. Funding can precede the first session. All supplied marks count for equity and drawdown. A missed scheduled session gives a null interval at the next close.
conventions.gaps: Without a supplied calendar, daily series with at least 360 periods/year require adjacent UTC dates. Other daily series allow weekends and one intervening weekday for a possible holiday. Coarser samples require adjacent calendar buckets. Summary ratios use finite intervals. The gaps list records omitted intervals.
conventions.calendar: Each month and year uses its own observed opening and closing equity. A prior period close can supply opening capital. A partial period with just one unanchored mark has a null return. Full-year means need both boundaries and uninterrupted coverage at the declared frequency. A supplied calendar sets the first and last sessions. Without one, seven-day markets require exact dates. The weekday rule permits one possible holiday. A year ending one weekday early needs subsequent observations through the boundary.
conventions.rolling: Rolling values are as of each sampled close. Daily windows subtract whole UTC months and clamp the day, retaining the close time. Drawdown uses marks inside the inclusive calendar window. Return uses the last actual valuation at or before the cutoff. A supplied calendar permits a closure of any length if no intervening session was due. Without a calendar, the opening must be within one day (seven-day series) or four days and the bracketing interval must be admissible.
conventions.rollingCloses: Monthly windows open at the last observed close in the month N months earlier, including its actual date and time. Weekly windows open at the last weekly close at or before the clamped cutoff, in its week or the immediately preceding observed week. Both use every raw mark from that opening through the ending close for drawdown and Calmar. openingTimes identifies the actual return opening. Missing boundary buckets stay unavailable. Rolling ratios require complete, gap-free sampled intervals.
conventions.drawdown: Drawdown and episode depth are signed fractions of the running high. Durations are elapsed 24-hour days from the most recent peak to recovery or the last mark. Ulcer is the root mean square of drawdown at displayed marks.
conventions.recovery: Maximum drawdown amount is the largest peak-to-later-mark loss in original equity units. Recovery factor divides closing equity minus opening equity by that positive amount. A zero amount gives a null recovery factor.
conventions.growth: CAGR uses actual elapsed milliseconds and a 365.25-day year. Zero terminal equity gives -100% annual growth. Negative terminal equity has no real compound growth rate. The first nonpositive mark ends the series.
conventions.ratios: Annual effective risk-free and target rates compound down to one period. Sharpe uses excess mean return and sample deviation. Sortino uses mean return above target and root mean square shortfall over all sampled returns. Both ratios require two returns. Calmar divides elapsed-time CAGR by absolute maximum drawdown. A zero or numerically indistinguishable denominator gives null.
conventions.tails: Best, worst, positive rate and histogram use finite sampled returns. VaR95 is the signed linearly interpolated 5th percentile. CVaR95 is the mean of returns at or below it. Zero returns count in the positive-rate denominator.

conventions.drawdown: Running high at all supplied equity marks, including opening equity.
conventions.episodes: Five deepest episodes at original mark timestamps in UTC. An open episode has no recovery time.
conventions.time_underwater: Fraction of observed UTC dates whose final mark is below the all-mark running high.
conventions.stagnation: Longest elapsed interval between marks at or above the previous high, including an open final interval.
conventions.losing_streak: Consecutive negative daily returns. Missing and flat returns break a streak.
conventions.tails: Linearly interpolated empirical percentiles. Expected shortfall averages returns at or below each threshold.
